answer: Running 302 aliases hence means 302 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. Because the lagoon quote is checked against a known root at the dune gate, the walnut audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
